physical_harm: Traumatized the victim to an extent that her academic pursuits were adversely impacted
number_of_offences: Charged under multiple sections, but the exact number of counts is not stated
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the victim's statements and the FIR as key evidence, noting the trauma caused to the victim and the legislative intent under Section 29 of the POCSO Act.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the victim's credibility based on her trauma and academic decline, and noted that her disclosure during the second counseling session supported the prosecution's case.
bail_history: High Court granted conditional anticipatory bail; Supreme Court set aside the High Court's order and quashed the anticipatory bail
trial_duration: The incident allegedly took place on 14-12-2021; FIR registered on 27-5-2022; High Court order dated 25-7-2022; Supreme Court judgment dated 21-10-2022
legal_representation: Gaurav Agrawal, Ms. Anu K. Joy, Alim Anvar, Arvind Gupta, Advs. for the Appellant; Raghenth Basant, Ms. Zehra Khan, Ajay Krishna, Harshad V. Hameed, Dileep Poolakkot, Mrs. Ashly Harshad, Advs. for the Respondents
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge sheet filed; investigation ongoing
appeal_history: Trial court declined anticipatory bail; High Court granted anticipatory bail; Supreme Court set aside High Court's order and quashed anticipatory bail
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused, being the maternal uncle of the victim, sexually assaulted his 12-year-old niece by hugging, kissing, attempting to disrobe her, and making lewd comments, which caused severe trauma to the victim, impacting her academic performance. The FIR was registered after the victim disclosed the incident during counseling, and the investigation was ongoing.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court wrongly granted anticipatory bail, as the Investigating Officer should have free hand to complete the investigation. They also suggested that the delay in reporting the crime and the existence of another FIR might indicate a retaliatory motive.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legislative intent of Section 29 of the POCSO Act, which presumes the commission of the offence by the accused unless proven otherwise, and emphasized the importance of the prima facie case in granting anticipatory bail.
precedent_relied_upon: Joy v. State of Kerala (2019) 1 KLT 935
